feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications/platform roles: the scope, progression, and public-sector specialization come through clearly. It is well written overall, but it feels slightly dense and repetitive, and a few style/grammar inconsistencies reduce polish.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, showing increasing leadership, ownership, and strategic scope over time.  
- Good use of scale and impact signals: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, named tools/platforms.  
- Strong positioning for modern digital leadership through a blend of strategy, governance, analytics, CMS, multimedia, and AI-enabled search.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; the overlap makes the CV longer without adding much value. Consolidating would improve structure and readability.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond activity descriptions, especially in the freelance role and recent projects (e.g., efficiency gains, engagement lifts, adoption, revenue/support outcomes).  
- Fix style consistency issues: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” “front-end” vs. other hyphenation choices, and list punctuation (some bullets use serial commas, some do not). Minor wording issue: “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary and weakens credibility slightly. No obvious misspellings; grammar is strong overall.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly dense and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience bullets. It would be stronger with one sharper value proposition and a few concrete signals of scale.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one sentence or two shorter sentences; reduce the long list of functions.
- Add a scale cue from recent work, e.g., “10,000+ page websites,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ publishers.”
- Replace “Leads” with “Led” or “Delivers” for tense consistency and clearer ownership.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing public-sector web platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume, mission-driven organizations. Delivers enterprise website transformation, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled user experiences at scale.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “editorial systems” repeat almost verbatim from Core Competencies and Work Experience.
- The subtitle already signals “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader,” so avoid restating the same positioning too closely.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize leadership-level capability areas rather than repeating detailed skill phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Reframe as broader, executive-level competencies: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and content operations • Analytics, reporting, and performance optimization • Multi-channel communications leadership
- Keep the most distinctive strengths tied to recent work: AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Standardize style for parallel structure; avoid mixing “systems,” “operations,” “infrastructure,” and “experiences” inconsistently
- Consider shortening to 6–8 items max and using “and” instead of “&” for a more polished, consistent tone

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “digital governance,” “analytics,” and “AI-enabled search” are already stated in the header and Topline Skills
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is repeated in Topline Skills and Work Experience
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with the recent consulting and NACo experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and format each item as a concise achievement, not a full sentence block.
- Use parallel phrasing and cleaner terms: “hybrid retrieval, vector search, and bill-level AI chat” is strong; consider “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” once only.
- Strengthen specificity where possible with scale or audience impact, e.g., campaign audience, number of modules/resources, or conference/event context.
- Revise for style consistency: “10 × 20-foot” (with spaces) and consider “main website” instead of “main site.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search and the microsite substantially repeat the current freelance role bullets.
- Advocacy Video Series overlaps with NACo experience describing the weekly advocacy video update and in-house video leadership.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Website

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around outcomes, leadership, and the highest-value themes not already covered elsewhere in the CV.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client context: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization in a full-time freelance engagement.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 sharper points; e.g., combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet focused on enterprise communications operations.
- Rephrase for outcomes: “Built Drupal campaign microsites, modular storytelling components, and member toolkits that improved campaign launch speed, content reuse, and cross-team publishing consistency.” Add metrics if available.
- Make the AI/search bullet more results-oriented: “Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and discovery UX.” If possible, add scope, launch status, or user impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” overlaps with the NACo Director role; emphasize new consulting ownership, client advisory scope, and AI/search work.
- Detailed project examples may duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry focused on role-level impact.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the most strategic outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad opener with a sharper scope statement: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Reorder bullets to lead with highest-impact achievements: website migration, analytics infrastructure, video studio, governance/operations.
- Make outcomes more concrete where possible: add launch timing, traffic/engagement gains, production cost savings, reporting efficiency, or turnaround improvements.
- Tighten channel bullet to emphasize leadership/results, not routine oversight: “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials and supporting advocacy and member engagement.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version strategic and outcome-focused.
- Video/programming language also echoes earlier NACo roles; emphasize building the studio and scaling in-house capability instead.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later NACo director role and the earlier digital media role. Tighten it to emphasize scope growth, editorial systems, and channel ownership at this mid-level stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to show advancement and scope: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Combine overlapping bullets and sharpen outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and durable: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing with systems language: “Improved editorial planning, cross-team coordination and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” overlap with the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this version focused on execution, not governance.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; frame this item as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent roles. Tighten it to emphasize distinctive leadership themes rather than repeating broad digital/comms language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-functional digital leadership” if you want stronger management emphasis.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie one skill to scale/complexity rather than listing only nouns, e.g., “Governance for high-volume, multi-publisher environments.”
- Keep wording parallel: all noun phrases, no mixed styles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” substantially duplicate Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” repeats the header and multiple NACo bullets; “communications” is broader and less repetitive.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix, but this item is too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and execution themes tied to recent Drupal/CMS modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from software inventory to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery” instead of listing every platform.
- Tighten to 6–8 items and prioritize recent strengths: Drupal, CMS modernization, front-end implementation, API/integration work, workflow automation, AI-enabled search.
- Move lower-priority or older/platform-specific tools like WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, Airtable, and jQuery to “Technical + IT” only.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and platform integrations • Workflow automation and operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating the same platform names in both sections.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; keep wording distinct or remove from one section.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it currently reads as a tool list and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic analytics capability and decision-making impact, not just platforms.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting and optimization” rather than a pure software inventory.
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” + “KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider stronger phrasing: replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboarding and decision support.”
- Suggested rewrite: “- Analytics infrastructure (GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity) - KPI framework design - Executive dashboarding and decision support - SEO, UX and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- Avoid adding A/B testing here unless you remove it from Technical + IT or can support it with experience evidence.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and older NACo bullets. Make it sharper, more senior, and tied to the strongest recent evidence: studio buildout, recurring video programming, and hybrid event delivery.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as outcome-oriented capabilities, not task labels: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations and PTZ camera systems • Multi-platform video editing and distribution”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to better reflect leadership-level scope.
- If space allows, add one credibility cue from recent work: “including in-house studio buildout and recurring advocacy programming.”
- Keep terms parallel and concise; avoid mixing tools, formats, and functions inconsistently.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; vary wording or remove one instance.
- “Studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” may feel too tactical unless balanced with higher-level phrasing like “studio and live production systems.”

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. In this section, make it more specific and weighted toward the platforms most relevant to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider signaling depth: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add scope rather than just names: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsites; multi-publisher governance) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV: use **Drupal 10** only if you mention versions elsewhere; otherwise stay platform-level.
- If this section is meant to be purely technical, consider dropping the weakest/least-used item if not supported elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel minor versus the seniority and enterprise focus of the CV unless tied to a real project.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more implementation-focused and align it to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize applied capability: “Front-End Development & Technical Implementation” or “Web Development & Integrations.”
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • REST/API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions (CI/CD)”
- If accurate, add scope or recency signals tied to recent roles/projects, e.g. “used for Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, automation, and deployment workflows.”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless needed; they date the section without adding value.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; either remove them there or make this section the detailed version.
- “GitHub Actions” may also overlap with workflow/automation language elsewhere; keep only if you’ve used it meaningfully in recent projects.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Workflow automation / Airtable systems” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize automation platforms over general collaboration tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to highlight systems capability, e.g. “Automation & Workflow Platforms: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana”
- Move Slack, Teams, and possibly Basecamp/Trello to a broader “Collaboration & Project Tools” line only if you need them elsewhere; they dilute the automation focus.
- Order by relevance/strength: put Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier first since they best support your recent consulting and digital operations work.
- If accurate, add scope instead of more tools: “workflow design,” “cross-platform automations,” or “editorial/project operations systems.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; keep this as a concise tool list, not another capability statement.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are partially redundant with each other; consider trimming to the platforms you’ve used most recently.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this should stay concise and tool-focused rather than restating channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform naming for readability and consistency: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add one capability cue to increase relevance without duplicating experience bullets, e.g.: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • newsletter operations • audience segmentation
- Keep the list ordered by strongest/recent enterprise relevance: Microsoft Dynamics 365 first, then Higher Logic, then Mailchimp

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding claims like “managed newsletters” or “led email strategy” here; those are already covered in Work Experience.
- If Higher Logic was the primary NACo platform, consider mentioning it in a recent role bullet instead of expanding this skills line too much.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Tighten it to emphasize analytics infrastructure and optimization methods most relevant to recent leadership work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Analytics & Optimization Tools
- Rewrite as: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI dashboards
- Replace “SEO” with “Google Search Console” or “SEO analysis” to keep this list tool/method-focused and more specific.
- If space allows, order by strategic weight/recency: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity, then optimization methods.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates “Topline Skills – Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider trimming one section or using this item for tools only while leaving KPI design/reporting in Topline Skills.
- “Dashboarding” is redundant with Looker Studio and Power BI; use “KPI dashboards” only if you want to signal outcome/application.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads as setup for later NACo roles. Tighten it around foundational impact, team-building, and channel execution without repeating achievements already covered in 2018–2024 entries.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make contributions more concrete: add scale if available for the website refresh, livestream program, or weekly video production cadence/audience.
- Sharpen leadership phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “supervised/mentored a digital media associate” if accurate.
- Suggested version: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, while mentoring a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating newsletter/editorial coordination language from the Associate Communications Director role.
- Don’t overstate video program ownership if the later role already claims expansion of the weekly advocacy series.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or scope, while avoiding overlap with later digital/media roles at NACo.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize the standout achievement first: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy teams; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer action: “Produced multimedia and digital content supporting program communications and policy outreach.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audiences served, cross-functional teams supported, or types of projects delivered.
- Keep this entry lighter than later NACo roles since those already cover broader digital leadership and multimedia growth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later NACo entries; keep this focused on innovation/research support and the podcast launch.
- Avoid repeating video/livestream language already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful supporting skills, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and multiple work bullets. Make it more tool-specific and keep production capabilities in one place.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator”
- If you want light context, use a tighter label: “Adobe Creative Tools: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator”
- Move “Livestream studio workflows” and “Podcast production” to the skills section or leave them only in work experience, where they already carry more credibility and impact.
